title: Mechanics modelling assumptions
statement: The basic ideas of mathematical modelling as applied in Mechanics.
guidance: Students should be familiar with the terms: particle, lamina, rigid body, rod (light, uniform, non-uniform), inextensible string, smooth and rough surface, light smooth pulley, bead, wire, peg. Students should be familiar with the assumptions made in using these models.

title: Magnitude, direction and resultant vectors
statement: Magnitude and direction of a vector. Resultant of vectors may also be required.
guidance: Students may be required to resolve a vector into two components or use a vector diagram. Questions may be set involving the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.

title: Vectors for displacement, velocity, force
statement: Application of vectors to displacements, velocities, accelerations and forces in a plane.
guidance: Use of $\text{velocity} = \dfrac{\text{change of displacement}}{\text{time}}$ in the case of constant velocity, and of $\text{acceleration} = \dfrac{\text{change of velocity}}{\text{time}}$ in the case of constant acceleration, will be required.

title: Constant acceleration in a straight line
statement: Motion in a straight line with constant acceleration.
guidance: Graphical solutions may be required, including displacement-time, velocity-time, speed-time and acceleration-time graphs. Knowledge and use of formulae for constant acceleration will be required.

title: Newton's laws of motion
statement: The concept of a force. Newton's laws of motion.
guidance: Simple problems involving constant acceleration in scalar form or as a vector of the form $a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j}$.

title: Connected particles and inclined planes
statement: Simple applications including the motion of two connected particles.
guidance: Problems may include: (i) the motion of two connected particles moving in a straight line or under gravity when the forces on each particle are constant; problems involving smooth fixed pulleys and/or pegs may be set; (ii) motion under a force which changes from one fixed value to another, e.g. a particle hitting the ground; (iii) motion directly up or down a smooth or rough inclined plane.

title: Momentum, impulse and collisions
statement: Momentum and impulse. The impulse-momentum principle. The principle of conservation of momentum applied to two particles colliding directly.
guidance: Knowledge of Newton's law of restitution is not required. Problems will be confined to those of a one-dimensional nature.

title: Coefficient of friction in motion
statement: Coefficient of friction.
guidance: An understanding of $F = \mu R$ when a particle is moving.

title: Resolving forces as vectors
statement: Forces treated as vectors. Resolution of forces.

title: Equilibrium of a particle
statement: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces. Weight, normal reaction, tension and thrust, friction.
guidance: Only simple cases of the application of the conditions for equilibrium to uncomplicated systems will be required.

title: Friction in equilibrium
statement: Coefficient of friction.
guidance: An understanding of $F \le \mu R$ in a situation of equilibrium.

title: Moments and equilibrium of a body
statement: Moment of a force.
guidance: Simple problems involving coplanar parallel forces acting on a body and conditions for equilibrium in such situations.

title: Modelling in probability and statistics
statement: The basic ideas of mathematical modelling as applied in probability and statistics.

title: Histograms, stem-and-leaf, box plots
statement: Histograms, stem and leaf diagrams, box plots.
guidance: Using histograms, stem and leaf diagrams and box plots to compare distributions. Back-to-back stem and leaf diagrams may be required. Drawing of histograms, stem and leaf diagrams or box plots will not be the direct focus of examination questions.

title: Mean, median and mode
statement: Measures of location – mean, median, mode.
guidance: Calculation of mean, mode and median, range and interquartile range will not be the direct focus of examination questions. Students will be expected to draw simple inferences and give interpretations to measures of location and dispersion. Significance tests will not be expected. Data may be discrete, continuous, grouped or ungrouped. Understanding and use of coding.

title: Variance, standard deviation, IQR
statement: Measures of dispersion – variance, standard deviation, range and interpercentile ranges.
guidance: Simple interpolation may be required. Interpretation of measures of location and dispersion.

title: Skewness and outliers
statement: Skewness. Concepts of outliers.
guidance: Students may be asked to illustrate the location of outliers on a box plot. Any rule to identify outliers will be specified in the question.

title: Elementary probability
statement: Elementary probability.

title: Conditional and complementary probability
statement: Sample space. Exclusive and complementary events. Conditional probability.
guidance: Understanding and use of $P(A') = 1 - P(A)$, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B \mid A)$.

title: Independent events
statement: Independence of two events.
guidance: $P(B \mid A) = P(B)$, $P(A \mid B) = P(A)$, $P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)$.

title: Tree diagrams and Venn diagrams
statement: Sum and product laws.
guidance: Use of tree diagrams and Venn diagrams. Sampling with and without replacement.

title: Linear regression by least squares
statement: Scatter diagrams. Linear regression. Calculation of the equation of a linear regression line using the method of least squares.
guidance: Students may be required to draw this regression line on a scatter diagram.

title: Explanatory and response variables
statement: Explanatory (independent) and response (dependent) variables. Applications and interpretations.
guidance: Use to make predictions within the range of values of the explanatory variable and the dangers of extrapolation. Derivations will not be required. Variables other than $x$ and $y$ may be used. Linear change of variable may be required.

title: Product moment correlation coefficient
statement: The product moment correlation coefficient, its use, interpretation and limitations.
guidance: Derivations and tests of significance will not be required.

title: Discrete random variable
statement: The concept of a discrete random variable.

title: Probability and cumulative distribution functions
statement: The probability function and the cumulative distribution function for a discrete random variable.
guidance: Simple uses of the probability function $p(x)$ where $p(x) = P(X = x)$. Use of the cumulative distribution function $F(x_0) = P(X \le x_0) = \sum_{x \le x_0} p(x)$.

title: Mean and variance of a discrete RV
statement: Mean and variance of a discrete random variable.
guidance: Use of $E(X)$, $E(X^2)$ for calculating the variance of $X$. Knowledge and use of $E(aX+b) = aE(X)+b$, $\operatorname{Var}(aX+b) = a^2\operatorname{Var}(X)$.

title: Discrete uniform distribution
statement: The discrete uniform distribution.
guidance: The mean and variance of this distribution.

title: The Normal distribution
statement: The Normal distribution including the mean, variance and use of tables of the cumulative distribution function.
guidance: Knowledge of the shape and the symmetry of the distribution is required. Knowledge of the probability density function is not required. Derivation of the mean, variance and cumulative distribution function is not required. Interpolation is not necessary. Questions may involve the solution of simultaneous equations.

title: Binomial and Poisson distributions
statement: The binomial and Poisson distributions.
guidance: Students will be expected to use these distributions to model a real-world situation and to comment critically on their appropriateness. Cumulative probabilities by calculation or by reference to tables. Students will be expected to use the additive property of the Poisson distribution, e.g. if the number of events per minute $\sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$ then the number of events per 5 minutes $\sim \text{Po}(5\lambda)$.

title: Mean and variance of binomial, Poisson
statement: The mean and variance of the binomial and Poisson distributions.
guidance: No derivations will be required.

title: Poisson approximation to binomial
statement: The use of the Poisson distribution as an approximation to the binomial distribution.

title: Continuous random variable
statement: The concept of a continuous random variable.

title: Probability density and distribution functions
statement: The probability density function and the cumulative distribution function for a continuous random variable.
guidance: Use of the probability density function $f(x)$, where $P(a < X \le b) = \displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$. Use of the cumulative distribution function $F(x_0) = P(X \le x_0) = \displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{x_0} f(x)\,dx$. The formulae used in defining $f(x)$ will be restricted to simple polynomials which may be expressed piecewise.

title: Relating pdf and cdf
statement: Relationship between density and distribution functions.
guidance: $f(x) = \dfrac{dF(x)}{dx}$.

title: Mean and variance of a continuous RV
statement: Mean and variance of continuous random variables.

title: Mode, median, quartiles of a continuous RV
statement: Mode, median and quartiles of continuous random variables.

title: Continuous uniform distribution
statement: The continuous uniform (rectangular) distribution.
guidance: Including the derivation of the mean, variance and cumulative distribution function.

title: Normal approximation with continuity correction
statement: Use of the Normal distribution as an approximation to the binomial distribution and the Poisson distribution, with the application of the continuity correction.

title: Population, census and sampling frame
statement: Population, census and sample. Sampling unit, sampling frame.
guidance: Students will be expected to know the advantages and disadvantages associated with a census and a sample survey.

title: Statistic and sampling distribution
statement: Concepts of a statistic and its sampling distribution.

title: Hypothesis test, null and alternative
statement: Concept and interpretation of a hypothesis test. Null and alternative hypotheses.
guidance: Use of hypothesis tests for refinement of mathematical models.

title: Critical region and test statistic
statement: Critical region.
guidance: Use of a statistic as a test statistic.

title: One-tailed and two-tailed tests
statement: One-tailed and two-tailed tests.

title: Hypothesis tests for p and Poisson mean
statement: Hypothesis tests for the parameter p of a binomial distribution and for the mean of a Poisson distribution.
guidance: Students are expected to know how to use tables to carry out these tests. Questions may also be set not involving tabular values. Tests for the parameter $p$ of a binomial distribution may involve the use of a normal approximation to calculate probabilities.

title: Linear combinations of Normal variables
statement: Distribution of linear combinations of independent Normal random variables.
guidance: If $X \sim N(\mu_x, \sigma_x^2)$ and $Y \sim N(\mu_y, \sigma_y^2)$ independently, then $aX \pm bY \sim N(a\mu_x \pm b\mu_y,\ a^2\sigma_x^2 + b^2\sigma_y^2)$. No proofs required.

title: Simple random sampling
statement: Methods for collecting data. Simple random sampling. Use of random numbers for sampling.

title: Stratified, systematic, quota sampling
statement: Other methods of sampling: stratified, systematic, quota.
guidance: The circumstances in which they might be used. Their advantages and disadvantages.

title: Standard error, estimator, bias
statement: Concepts of standard error, estimator, bias.
guidance: The sample mean, $\bar{x}$, and the sample variance, $s^2 = \dfrac{1}{n-1}\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2$, as unbiased estimates of the corresponding population parameters.

title: Distribution of the sample mean
statement: The distribution of the sample mean $\bar{X}$.
guidance: $\bar X$ has mean $\mu$ and variance $\dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}$. If $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ then $\bar X \sim N\left(\mu, \dfrac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)$. No proofs required.

title: Confidence interval concept
statement: Concept of a confidence interval and its interpretation.
guidance: Link with hypothesis tests.

title: Confidence interval for a Normal mean
statement: Confidence limits for a Normal mean, with variance known.
guidance: Students will be expected to know how to apply the Normal distribution and use the standard error and obtain confidence intervals for the mean, rather than be concerned with any theoretical derivations.

title: Hypothesis test for a Normal mean
statement: Hypothesis tests for the mean of a Normal distribution with variance known.
guidance: Use of $\dfrac{\bar X - \mu}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \sim N(0,1)$.

title: Central Limit Theorem for large samples
statement: Use of Central Limit theorem to extend hypothesis tests and confidence intervals to samples from non-Normal distributions. Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the variance is unknown.
guidance: $\dfrac{\bar X - \mu}{S/\sqrt{n}}$ can be treated as $N(0,1)$ when $n$ is large. A knowledge of the $t$-distribution is not required.

title: Comparing two Normal means, variances known
statement: Hypothesis test for the difference between the means of two Normal distributions with variances known.
guidance: Use of $\dfrac{(\bar X - \bar Y) - (\mu_x - \mu_y)}{\sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma_x^2}{n_x} + \dfrac{\sigma_y^2}{n_y}}} \sim N(0,1)$.

title: Comparing two means, variances unknown
statement: Use of large sample results to extend to the case in which the population variances are unknown.
guidance: Use of $\dfrac{(\bar X - \bar Y) - (\mu_x - \mu_y)}{\sqrt{\dfrac{S_x^2}{n_x} + \dfrac{S_y^2}{n_y}}} \sim N(0,1)$. A knowledge of the $t$-distribution is not required.

title: Chi-squared goodness of fit statistic
statement: The null and alternative hypotheses. The use of $\sum_{i=1}^n \dfrac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}$ as an approximate $\chi^2$ statistic.
guidance: Applications to include the discrete uniform, binomial, Normal, Poisson and continuous uniform (rectangular) distributions. Lengthy calculations will not be required.

title: Degrees of freedom
statement: Degrees of freedom.
guidance: Students will be expected to determine the degrees of freedom when one or more parameters are estimated from the data. Cells should be combined when $E_i < 5$. Yates' correction is not required.

title: Spearman's rank correlation
statement: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, its use, interpretation and limitations.
guidance: Numerical questions involving ties will not be set. Some understanding of how to deal with ties will be expected.

title: Testing for zero correlation
statement: Testing the hypothesis that a correlation is zero.
guidance: Use of tables for Spearman's and product moment correlation coefficients.

title: Algorithms as flow charts or text
statement: The general ideas of algorithms and the implementation of an algorithm given by a flow chart or text.
guidance: The order of an algorithm is not expected. Whenever finding the middle item of any list, the method defined in the glossary must be used: the middle item of a list of $N$ items is at position $\left[\tfrac{1}{2}(N+1)\right]$ if $N$ is odd, and $\left[\tfrac{1}{2}(N+2)\right]$ if $N$ is even.

title: Bin packing and sorting algorithms
statement: Students should be familiar with bin packing, bubble sort, quick sort, binary search.
guidance: When using the quick sort algorithm, the pivot should be chosen as the middle item of the list.

title: Minimum spanning tree algorithms
statement: The minimum spanning tree (minimum connector) problem. Prim's and Kruskal's algorithm.
guidance: Matrix representation for Prim's algorithm is expected. Drawing a network from a given matrix and writing down the matrix associated with a network will be involved.

title: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm
statement: Dijkstra's algorithm for finding the shortest path.

title: Route inspection (Chinese postman) problem
statement: Algorithm for finding the shortest route around a network, travelling along every edge at least once and ending at the start vertex. The network will have up to four odd nodes.
guidance: Also known as the 'Chinese postman' problem. Students will be expected to use inspection to consider all possible pairings of odd nodes. (The application of Floyd's algorithm to the odd nodes is not required.)

title: Travelling salesman problem
statement: The practical and classical Travelling Salesman problems. The classical problem for complete graphs satisfying the triangle inequality.
guidance: The use of short cuts to improve upper bound is included.

title: Upper and lower bounds for TSP
statement: Determination of upper and lower bounds using minimum spanning tree methods.
guidance: The conversion of a network into a complete network of shortest 'distances' is included.

title: Nearest neighbour algorithm
statement: The nearest neighbour algorithm.

title: Activity networks from precedence tables
statement: Modelling of a project by an activity network, from a precedence table.
guidance: Activity on arc will be used. The use of dummies is included. In a precedence network, precedence tables will only show immediate predecessors.

title: Precedence tables from activity networks
statement: Completion of the precedence table for a given activity network.

title: Critical path algorithm
statement: Algorithm for finding the critical path. Earliest and latest event times. Earliest and latest start and finish times for activities.

title: Total float and Gantt charts
statement: Total float. Gantt (cascade) charts. Scheduling.
guidance: The total float $F(i,j)$ of activity $(i,j)$ is defined to be $F(i,j) = l_j - e_i - \text{duration}(i,j)$, where $e_i$ is the earliest time for event $i$ and $l_j$ is the latest time for event $j$.

title: Formulating linear programs
statement: Formulation of problems as linear programs.

title: Graphical solution of linear programs
statement: Graphical solution of two variable problems using ruler and vertex methods.

title: Integer solutions to linear programs
statement: Consideration of problems where solutions must have integer values.
